Contributions to percent change of chain-linked volume measures

Source: vignettes/contributions.Rmd
contributions.Rmd
library(chainlink)

Chain-linked volume measures are not additive, so that the contribution of a component to the growth of the total cannot be read from the growth of the components. chain_contrib() computes exact contributions: they add up to the growth of the total (up to the inconsistencies of the data, see below). The formulas follow the chapter 8 of the IMF Quarterly National Accounts Manual (paragraphs 8.86-8.90).

Principle

Let xi,tx_{i,t} be the chain volume measure (in monetary terms) of the component ii in period tt, ztz_t the one of the total, and y(t)y(t) the year of the period tt. Within a year yy, the chain volume measure of the total is exactly the sum of the chain volume measures of the components, valued at the relative prices ρi,y−1\rho_{i,y-1} of the previous year: zt=∑iρi,y(t)−1xi,t. z_t = \sum_i \rho_{i,y(t)-1}\, x_{i,t}. The relative price ρi,y\rho_{i,y} is the implicit price of the component ii over the implicit price of the total:

  • annual overlap (method = "ao"), with the annual sums cpi,ycp_{i,y}, xi,yx_{i,y}, cpycp_y and zyz_y of the current prices and of the chain volume measures: ρi,y=cpi,y/xi,ycpy/zy; \rho_{i,y} = \frac{cp_{i,y} / x_{i,y}}{cp_y / z_y};
  • one-quarter overlap (method = "oqo"): the same ratio computed on the overlap period (the last quarter, or the last month, of year yy), the current prices being valued at the average prices of the year (cp_pi2cy()).

The contribution of the component ii to the growth between a period ss and a period tt (previous period, same period of the previous year, or previous year) is Ci,t=100[(xi,t−xi,s)ρi,y(t)−1zs+(xi,szs−ai,y(t)−1)(ρi,y(t)−1−ρi,y(s)−1)] C_{i,t} = 100 \left[\frac{(x_{i,t} - x_{i,s})\,\rho_{i,y(t)-1}}{z_s} + \left(\frac{x_{i,s}}{z_s} - a_{i,y(t)-1}\right) \left(\rho_{i,y(t)-1} - \rho_{i,y(s)-1}\right)\right] where ai,ya_{i,y} is the share of the component in the total: ai,y=xi,y/zya_{i,y} = x_{i,y} / z_y (annual sums) for the annual overlap, and the same share on the overlap period for the one-quarter overlap. Summing over ii gives ∑iCi,t=100(zt/zs−1)\sum_i C_{i,t} = 100\,(z_t / z_s - 1).

The second term is zero if ss and tt are in the same year. For the annual overlap and the growth over the previous period, this is the formula of the example 8.9 of the manual. The formula for the one-quarter overlap, and for the growth over the same period of the previous year, derive from the same decomposition: they add up to the growth of the total exactly.

The breakdown between the components is not unique, only its sum is: the second term (revaluation due to the change of relative prices) is allocated as in the manual.

Example

chain_laspeyres() computes the chain volume measures of the components and of their total (last column):

x <- chain_laspeyres(imf_cp, imf_pi, method = "ao", base_year = 2010,
                     output = "measure")
round(x, 3)
#>               A       B   Total
#> 2011 Q1 156.569 221.111 377.680
#> 2011 Q2 159.220 218.061 377.281
#> 2011 Q3 162.524 214.898 377.422
#> 2011 Q4 164.757 213.838 378.596
#> 2012 Q1 165.592 213.614 379.379
#> 2012 Q2 172.326 206.530 379.313
#> 2012 Q3 182.232 198.199 381.269
#> 2012 Q4 206.869 176.073 384.751
#> 2013 Q1 214.161 171.375 388.616
#> 2013 Q2 226.999 159.763 390.766
#> 2013 Q3 235.015 151.043 390.688
#> 2013 Q4 238.639 146.558 390.128

Contributions to the growth over the previous quarter (type = "period", the default). extra adds the growth of the total and the residual (growth of the total minus the sum of the contributions):

chain_contrib(x, imf_cp, method = "ao", extra = c("total", "residual")) |>
    round(3)
#>             A      B  Total Residual
#> 2011 Q1    NA     NA     NA       NA
#> 2011 Q2 0.702 -0.808 -0.106        0
#> 2011 Q3 0.876 -0.838  0.038        0
#> 2011 Q4 0.592 -0.281  0.311        0
#> 2012 Q1 0.248 -0.041  0.207        0
#> 2012 Q2 1.817 -1.835 -0.017        0
#> 2012 Q3 2.673 -2.158  0.516        0
#> 2012 Q4 6.615 -5.701  0.913        0
#> 2013 Q1 2.082 -1.077  1.005        0
#> 2013 Q2 3.440 -2.887  0.553        0
#> 2013 Q3 2.136 -2.156 -0.020        0
#> 2013 Q4 0.966 -1.109 -0.143        0

Contributions to the growth over the same quarter of the previous year:

chain_contrib(x, imf_cp, method = "ao", type = "yoy", extra = "total") |>
    round(3)
#>              A       B Total
#> 2011 Q1     NA      NA    NA
#> 2011 Q2     NA      NA    NA
#> 2011 Q3     NA      NA    NA

Contributions to the growth of the annual sums:

chain_contrib(x, imf_cp, method = "ao", type = "annual", extra = "total") |>
    round(3)
#> Time Series:
#> Start = 2011 
#> End = 2013 
#> Frequency = 1 
#>           A       B Total
#> 2011  2.871  -2.139 0.732
#> 2012  5.687  -4.779 0.909

One-quarter overlap 

x_oqo <- chain_laspeyres(imf_cp, imf_pi, method = "oqo", base_year = 2010,
                         output = "measure")
chain_contrib(x_oqo, imf_cp, method = "oqo", type = "period", pi = imf_pi,
              extra = c("total", "residual")) |>
    round(3)
#>             A      B  Total Residual
#> 2011 Q1    NA     NA     NA       NA
#> 2011 Q2 0.702 -0.808 -0.106        0
#> 2011 Q3 0.876 -0.838  0.038        0
#> 2011 Q4 0.592 -0.281  0.311        0
#> 2012 Q1 0.226 -0.058  0.167        0
#> 2012 Q2 1.817 -1.835 -0.017        0
#> 2012 Q3 2.673 -2.158  0.516        0
#> 2012 Q4 6.615 -5.701  0.913        0
#> 2013 Q1 1.970 -1.177  0.792        0
#> 2013 Q2 3.440 -2.887  0.553        0
#> 2013 Q3 2.136 -2.156 -0.020        0
#> 2013 Q4 0.966 -1.109 -0.143        0

The overlap quarter is valued at the average prices of the year, as in the manual (cp_pi2cy()): chain_contrib() needs the price indices pi to do so (or cp already valued at these prices). With the one-quarter overlap technique, the contributions to the annual growth are only available from the second year (the annual sum of the base year is not defined).

Correspondence with the manual

  • annual overlap: type = "period" and type = "annual" are the equations (29) (quarters 2 to 4 and annual data) and (30) (first quarter) of the paragraphs 8.86-8.87, and type = "yoy" is the equation (31) of the paragraph 8.88. The example 8.9 is reproduced by the tests of the package;
  • one-quarter overlap: the manual (footnote 35) applies the same formulas with the annual deflators, but the contributions are then not exactly additive. The package provides this variant with method = "ao" applied to the one-quarter overlap measures, and an exactly additive version with method = "oqo":
x_oqo <- chain_laspeyres(imf_cp, imf_pi, method = "oqo", base_year = 2010,
                         output = "measure")
# Formulas of the manual (annual deflators)
chain_contrib(x_oqo, imf_cp, method = "ao", extra = "residual") |> round(4)
#>              A       B Residual
#> 2011 Q1     NA      NA       NA
#> 2011 Q2 0.7019 -0.8075   0.0000
#> 2011 Q3 0.8759 -0.8384   0.0000
#> 2011 Q4 0.5916 -0.2807   0.0000
#> 2012 Q1 0.2483 -0.0414  -0.0396
#> 2012 Q2 1.8178 -1.8353   0.0000
#> 2012 Q3 2.6745 -2.1586  -0.0002
#> 2012 Q4 6.6174 -5.7037  -0.0004
#> 2013 Q1 2.0792 -1.0746  -0.2124
#> 2013 Q2 3.4476 -2.8932  -0.0012
#> 2013 Q3 2.1408 -2.1609   0.0000
#> 2013 Q4 0.9681 -1.1116   0.0003
# Deflators of the overlap period (valued at the average prices of the year)
chain_contrib(x_oqo, imf_cp, method = "oqo", pi = imf_pi,
              extra = "residual") |> round(4)
#>              A       B Residual
#> 2011 Q1     NA      NA       NA
#> 2011 Q2 0.7019 -0.8075        0
#> 2011 Q3 0.8759 -0.8384        0
#> 2011 Q4 0.5916 -0.2807        0
#> 2012 Q1 0.2255 -0.0582        0
#> 2012 Q2 1.8171 -1.8346        0
#> 2012 Q3 2.6734 -2.1578        0
#> 2012 Q4 6.6148 -5.7014        0
#> 2013 Q1 1.9696 -1.1774        0
#> 2013 Q2 3.4403 -2.8871        0
#> 2013 Q3 2.1363 -2.1563        0
#> 2013 Q4 0.9660 -1.1093        0
  • a variable that can be negative, zero or positive (changes in inventories) is treated residually (paragraph 8.90): its contribution is the difference between the contribution of the aggregate that includes it and the contributions of the other components.

Quarterly Fisher indices

The paragraph 8.89 gives the contributions to the percent change of a quarterly Fisher index. fisher_contrib() takes the current prices of all the components and their price indices over the previous quarter (pi_py2pp() converts price indices over the previous year):

ep8.4 <- pi_py2pp(imf_pi)
fisher_contrib(imf_cp, ep8.4, extra = c("total", "residual")) |> round(3)
#>             A      B  Total Residual
#> 2010 Q1    NA     NA     NA       NA
#> 2010 Q2    NA     NA     NA       NA
#> 2010 Q3    NA     NA     NA       NA
#> 2010 Q4    NA     NA     NA       NA
#> 2011 Q1 1.767 -1.031  0.737        0
#> 2011 Q2 0.717 -0.795 -0.078        0
#> 2011 Q3 0.900 -0.822  0.078        0
#> 2011 Q4 0.607 -0.275  0.331        0
#> 2012 Q1 0.232 -0.057  0.175        0
#> 2012 Q2 1.860 -1.800  0.060        0
#> 2012 Q3 2.713 -2.130  0.583        0
#> 2012 Q4 6.699 -5.632  1.068        0
#> 2013 Q1 1.951 -1.195  0.756        0
#> 2013 Q2 3.433 -2.895  0.538        0
#> 2013 Q3 2.119 -2.182 -0.063        0
#> 2013 Q4 0.955 -1.130 -0.175        0

With xitx_i^t the current price value of the component ii in period tt, ztz^t the one of the aggregate, ri=pit/pit−1r_i = p_i^t / p_i^{t-1} the price index of the component over the previous period and FF the Fisher volume index of the aggregate (previous period = 1), the contribution of the component ii is Cit=100ztzt−1(xitri−xit−1)+F(xit−xit−1ri)zt+F∑jxjt−1rj. C_i^t = 100\, \frac{\dfrac{z^t}{z^{t-1}} \left(\dfrac{x_i^t}{r_i} - x_i^{t-1}\right) + F \left(x_i^t - x_i^{t-1} r_i\right)} {z^t + F \sum_j x_j^{t-1} r_j}.

This is the equation (32) of the manual. The decomposition is exact: the residual is zero up to numerical errors. As printed in the manual, the equation has the ratio zt−1/ztz^{t-1} / z^t in the first term and xit−1/rix_i^{t-1} / r_i in the second one; with these ratios, the contributions do not add up to the percent change. The version implemented uses zt/zt−1z^t / z^{t-1} and xit−1rix_i^{t-1} r_i (consistent with the denominator). The adjustments that some countries add to the quarterly contributions (benchmarking of the quarterly indices, annual rates) are not done.

Non-additivity and residual

Two different things must not be mixed up:

  • the chain volume measures are not additive: the chain measure of the total is not the sum of the chain measures of the components. chain_discrepancy() returns Dt=∑ixi,t−ztD_t = \sum_i x_{i,t} - z_t (or 100Dt/zt100\, D_t / z_t with relative = TRUE). It is zero in the base year and, with the annual overlap, in the year after;
  • the contributions take this into account and add up to the growth of the total. The residual (extra = "residual") is therefore zero if the data are fully consistent, i.e. if the annual price indices are exactly those of the quarterly data. In the example of the manual, they are not (the residual is small, below 0.001 percentage point).
chain_discrepancy(x) |> round(3)
#>        Qtr1   Qtr2   Qtr3   Qtr4
#> 2011  0.000  0.000  0.000  0.000
#> 2012 -0.173 -0.457 -0.837 -1.809
#> 2013 -3.080 -4.004 -4.630 -4.932
chain_discrepancy(x, relative = TRUE) |> round(3)
#>        Qtr1   Qtr2   Qtr3   Qtr4
#> 2011  0.000  0.000  0.000  0.000
#> 2012 -0.046 -0.120 -0.220 -0.470
#> 2013 -0.793 -1.025 -1.185 -1.264

Monthly data

The functions use the frequency of the series. As an illustration, each quarter of the data of the example is spread over three months (the contributions are then non-zero only for the first month of each quarter, when the quarter changes):

spread <- function(a, scale = 1) {
    m <- as.matrix(a)
    res <- ts(m[rep(seq_len(nrow(m)), each = 3), , drop = FALSE] * scale,
              start = c(start(a)[1], 1), frequency = 12)
    colnames(res) <- colnames(a)
    res
}
cp_m <- spread(imf_cp, 1 / 3)
pi_m <- spread(imf_pi)
x_m <- chain_laspeyres(cp_m, pi_m, method = "ao", base_year = 2010,
                       output = "measure")
chain_contrib(x_m, cp_m, method = "ao") |>
    window(start = c(2011, 1), end = c(2011, 8)) |>
    round(3)
#>              A      B
#> Jan 2011    NA     NA
#> Feb 2011 0.000  0.000
#> Mar 2011 0.000  0.000
#> Apr 2011 0.702 -0.808
#> May 2011 0.000  0.000
#> Jun 2011 0.000  0.000
#> Jul 2011 0.876 -0.838
#> Aug 2011 0.000  0.000

Variables that change sign

Growth rates and chain volume measures are meaningless for a variable that can be negative, zero or positive, such as changes in inventories (paragraph 8.56 of the manual). Two solutions:

  • contributions are calculated residually (paragraph 8.90): the contribution of the variable is the difference between the contribution of the aggregate that includes it and the contributions of the other components;
  • a pseudo chain volume series is derived (paragraphs 8.57-8.58): the variable is written as the difference of two series that only take positive values (closing minus opening inventories, exports minus imports), each of them is chain-linked separately, and the chain volume series is their difference. chain_pseudo() does it, from the current prices and the price indices of the two series (the two products of the example below only stand in for them):
chain_pseudo(imf_cp[, "A"], imf_pi[, "A"],
             imf_cp[, "B"], imf_pi[, "B"], base_year = 2010) |> round(1)
#>       Qtr1  Qtr2  Qtr3  Qtr4
#> 2011 -64.5 -58.8 -52.4 -49.1
#> 2012 -48.0 -34.2 -16.0  30.8
#> 2013  42.8  67.2  84.0  92.1

Change of the reference year

chain_rebase() changes the reference year of an index or of a measure. With bb the new reference year and I‾b\bar{I}_b the average of the index over its periods, the rebased index is 100It/I‾b100\, I_t / \bar{I}_b; a measure is multiplied by cpb/xbcp_b / x_b (annual sums of the current prices and of the measure in year bb). The growth rates are unchanged.

chain_laspeyres(imf_cp, imf_pi, base_year = 2010) |>
    chain_rebase(base_year = 2012) |>
    round(2)
#>              A      B  Total
#> 2011 Q1  86.14 111.33  99.08
#> 2011 Q2  87.60 109.80  98.98
#> 2011 Q3  89.42 108.20  99.01
#> 2011 Q4  90.65 107.67  99.32
#> 2012 Q1  91.11 107.56  99.53
#> 2012 Q2  94.81 103.99  99.51
#> 2012 Q3 100.26  99.80 100.02
#> 2012 Q4 113.82  88.66 100.94
#> 2013 Q1 117.83  86.29 101.95
#> 2013 Q2 124.89  80.44 102.52
#> 2013 Q3 129.30  76.05 102.49
#> 2013 Q4 131.30  73.79 102.35
